# dsh-tui -- the DeepSeek Harness terminal UI plugin

`dsh-TUI` (https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI, npm
`@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`) is a **pure DSH plugin**, not a
daemon. It is added to a dsh *profile* and launched by the shipped
`dsh-tui` / `dst` launcher (or `dsh --profile dsh-tui`). The candy
`dsh-tui` composes the `dsh` CLI candy and adds the plugin + a typed
terminal channel.

## Candy Properties

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Install files | `charly.yml`, `package.json` |
| Depends | `dsh` (the CLI candy), `layer-tmux` |
| Env | `DSH_TUI_NO_LAUNCHPAD=1` (boot straight to the composer) |
| Channel | `terminal_profile: dsh-tui` + `agent_provide: tmux` |
| Profile | `$DSH_HOME/profiles/dsh-tui` (auto-bootstrapped on first launch) |

## Deterministic first launch

The first-run wizard is pre-recorded at `~/.dsh-tui/onboarding.json`
(`{"completed":true,"version":1}`) and the launchpad is disabled
(`DSH_TUI_NO_LAUNCHPAD=1`), so the process lands directly on the chat
screen with no keyboard-owning dialog — the state a terminal channel
can drive. Without both, an ordinary launch opens the wizard or the
launchpad, which own the keyboard.

## The terminal channel

The candy publishes a `terminal_profile` (entrypoint `dsh-tui`) and an
`agent_provide: {provider: tmux, profiles: [dsh-tui]}` capability. A
disposable bed or a host controller drives it through
`charly agent terminal launch/snapshot/input/key/transcript`. A
terminal channel is **on-demand**, not a long-running service: a
service-less box that carries it must be held at steady state by
`check-keepalive`'s `sleep infinity` supervisord program.

## Driving the channel deterministically

The channel is a real terminal, so it must be driven the way a
terminal behaves — not the way a service does:

- **Unique run-ids.** `launch`/`input`/`snapshot`/`close` are keyed by
  `--run-id`. A hardcoded run-id collides when `check-live` and
  `check-live-rebuild` run the same plan in one session; derive a
  fresh id per step (a `uuidgen`/`date +%s%N`-style value), never a
  literal.
- **`snapshot` is a render of the viewport, so it is scroll/cursor
  dependent** — a text that scrolled off is gone. To assert content,
  read the durable **`transcript`** (the full session log), not a
  snapshot taken at an arbitrary moment.
- **`close` closes the control channel, not the process.** The TUI
  keeps running under tmux after a `close`; do not rely on `close` to
  reap it, and never launch a second session against the same target
  while a first is still attached — two concurrent control sessions on
  one pod contend for the same tmux server.
- **The interactive submit is keyboard-timing racy.** Typing a prompt
  and injecting the submit key can race the TUI's redraw, so a
  pass/fail that depends on the enter landing is flaky by
  construction. An interactive TUI's *liveness* is proven by the
  channel (`launch` → non-empty `transcript` → `close`); the live
  model turn it fronts is asserted separately with a one-shot,
  non-interactive `dsh --headless` call in the same box.

## Usage

```yaml
# charly.yml
my-tui-box:
  candy:
    - dsh-tui
```

```bash
charly start my-tui-box
# drive the TUI through the channel:
charly agent terminal launch '{"name":"dsh-tui","entrypoint":["dsh-tui"],"cols":140,"rows":44,"keys":["enter"]}' --target my-tui-box --run-id <uuid>
```
